entries.title: AI Guard for Apps 10/16/2026
body: # Inbound Integrations
AI Guard now has a new Inbound Integrations page that allows third-party AI platforms to call AI Guard for a policy decision on every prompt and response.
See image.
The two integrations currently available are:

- Anthropic: Claude sends each prompt and response to AI Guard through inference hooks. This was previously supported on the Tenant Settings page, but has been moved to the new Inbound Integrations page. Existing Anthropic integrations from Tenant Settings will still work.

- To manage existing integrations on the new page: On the Inbound Integrations page, click Save here on a previously created integration, then click Save Integration to keep all setup information and have the integration managed from the Inbound Integrations page.
- Databricks (New): The Unity AI Gateway checks every governed model against AI Guard as an external guardrail policy.
To learn more, see Managing Inbound Integrations.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming AI App Diagnostics
body: AIRT introduces AI App Diagnostic to validate various aspects of the application prior to running a full probe. After working with many customers, we have found that configuration and integration issues were often discovered only after a probe run had started, which caused failed or blocked runs and misleading findings. This feature will perform various validation checks to minimize any setup issues.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming Policy Generator support for Azure Guardrails
body: Policy Generator now supports Azure Guardrails, enabling the direct generation of policies tailored to configured AI Apps. Each generated policy includes an API Request featuring the Azure Resource Manager command required to establish the content filter policy, alongside a JSON Formatted Policy that uses Azure's RAI policy schema for the request body.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming Zip File Support for MCP Server Analysis
body: MCP Server Analysis now supports ZIP archive uploads. This provides customers with the ability to test private MCP servers that aren't in public repositories.

entries.title: AI Guard for Apps 09/25/2026
body: # Audit Log UI Improvements
The Audit Log page in AI Guard has received the following upgrades:
- In the Initiator column, you will now see the username and email listed instead of just the email address.
- The initiator search functionality has been updated with a dropdown of usernames that can be selected.
- See image.
- A time range filter has been added with custom and preset ranges (Last 24 Hours, Last 7 Days, etc.).
- See image.
- The manual refresh button now reloads the list without reloading the entire page.
- The Export CSV button downloads the filtered audit log.
To learn more, see AI Guard Audit Log.
# Enhancements & Bug Fixes
- AI Guard now supports GitHub Copilot Enterprise in Visual Studio (VS) Code.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming Compliance Mapping
body: AIRT now maps test results to compliance frameworks.
The Compliance Mapping page gives you one tenant-wide view of your organization's posture across frameworks.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming MCP Server Analysis
body: MCP Server Analysis provides visibility into the security posture of MCP servers running in the customer's environment. The analysis can be performed on both open-source MCP servers and proprietary MCP servers. A related capability, MCP Security Ratings, provides a catalog of public MCP servers and the results that have been tested by Zscaler.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming System Information Leakage Probe
body: AIRT introduces a new security probe: System Information Leakage.

This new probe simulates attacks that try to make the target reveal the architecture behind it: the language model and provider it runs on, whether it is a single model or a multi-agent pipeline, the tools it calls, and the infrastructure it is deployed on. The probe combines direct questions, wrong guesses, role-play, and debugging pretexts with malformed inputs that trigger raw platform errors.

To learn more, see About AI Guard Dashboard and About AI Guard Detection Summary.

entries.title: GCP Single Project Onboarding
body: AI Security now supports the onboarding of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) single projects to monitor and scan the data stores within them. This option can be used when there are restrictions for onboarding projects at the organization level.
See image.
To learn more, see Onboarding a GCP Project.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming AI Prefill Modal
body: AIRT is most effective when it has the proper context about an application. However, it's often not easy to obtain this context. The new AI Prefill can help with obtaining this information. Once basic connectivity has been established, AI Prefill runs a short, automated workflow against the application. Based on the responses from the application, AI Prefill suggests the Application description, Language, Multi-step attacks, and Supported modes.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming Connection Type Categorization Updates
body: Changes have been made to the 'Connection Type' categorization to better align with integration functionality.
- API (No changes): REST API, PROXY SDK, OpenAI REST API.
- Platform (Updated): Now includes third-party model wrappers. Added: Poe, OpenRouter, Monica, You.com, Venice, Ask AI, and CrewAI.
- LLM: Reserved for direct model API integrations: Azure OpenAI, Azure ML, Anthropic, Databricks, Hugging Face, OpenAI, OpenAI Assistant, Mistral, Gemini, Bedrock, Grok, Kimi, and Perplexity.
- UI/UX Consolidation: 'You.com Research' and 'You.com Answer' have been merged into a single 'You.com' card with a mode toggle, matching the pattern used for Glean.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming Public Agent Skills Registry
body: AIRT introduces the agent skills registry where security ratings are provided to help organizations assess the safety of public agent skills before adoption. With this feature, customers can easily assess the risks and determine whether it's suitable for deployment in production.

entries.title: AI Guard for Apps 08/26/2026
body: # Additional CrowdStrike Log Export Option

AI Guard now supports a new log export destination, CrowdStrike SIEM Direct Export, alongside the existing S3-dependent CrowdStrike option. You can now choose between exporting directly to the CrowdStrike HEC endpoint or routing event content through an intermediary AWS S3 bucket, depending on your existing setup.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.
# New CrowdStrike Parser for AI Guard

CrowdStrike has updated their portal to include a new parser for AI Guard under the Generic bender connection type as zscaler-aiguard. This allows CrowdStrike users to select the AI Guard-specific parser when configuring a new data connector, rather than relying on the generic template parser.
See image.
# Enhancements & Bug Fixes

- Increased Topic Definition Character Limit: The character limit for Topic definitions in policy configuration has been increased from its previous limit to 1000 characters, giving admins more room to write detailed, precise topic definitions when building Topic policies.

- Expanded LLM Provider Match Criteria Limit: The LLM Provider field used for match criteria in Policy control now supports up to 100 entries, up from the previous limit of 10. This allows admins to define broader and more granular policies across a wider range of LLM providers without hitting capacity constraints.

- Policy Configuration Version Information: Detectors now include version information in the Policy Configuration UI in AI Guard, giving admins and security teams clearer visibility into which version of a detector is in use.
- Base64 Support for Detectors: All detectors now support base64.

entries.title: AI Guard for Apps 08/07/2026
body: # Event Log Export Tools Field Filter
Log exports can now be configured to filter out the Tools fields from exported event logs. This field is enabled by default for new and existing exports.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.
# Claude Inference Hook Integration

AI Guard can now integrate with Anthropic Claude's inference hooks to inspect and evaluate prompts against a tenant's detection policy in real time. AI Guard responds with an Allow or Deny verdict, which determines whether Claude proceeds to generate a response or the prompt is blocked.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Tenant Settings.
# Enhancements & Bug Fixes

- Malicious URL Detection in Prompt Policies: Malicious URLs can now be configured as a detection category within prompt detection policies on the policy configuration page. This expands your ability to identify and control URL-based threats embedded in user prompts.
- Pattern Detector Configuration Limit Increased: The Text (Pattern) detector now supports up to 100 regex patterns per policy, increased from the previous limit of 10.
- Regex Pattern Length Limit for Text Detector: Individual regex patterns in the Text (Pattern) detector can now be up to 3,000 characters in length, increased from the previous limit.

- CSV Export for Dashboard Events: Dashboard event tables now support CSV export in addition to the existing PDF export option. This provides greater flexibility when sharing, analyzing, or archiving flagged interactions.

entries.title: ServiceNow Integration for AI Security
body: AI Security now integrates with ServiceNow, enabling security, IT, and risk teams to sync AI Security-discovered assets and issues into existing governance and risk workflows. AI Security pushes discovered AI assets such as models, agents, MCP servers, data stores, workloads, software libraries, guardrails, code repositories, and identities into ServiceNow via Import Sets (staging tables). Your ServiceNow administrators control how staged data maps to production classes using Transform Maps.
As a part of this feature, the following changes are available in AI Security Admin Portal:
- One-way data push from AI Security to ServiceNow for all supported AI resource types and associated security issues.
- Scheduled synchronization to keep ServiceNow current with AI Security discoveries.
- Security issues surfaced as incidents, problems, or custom table records in ServiceNow, linked to the corresponding AI CIs.
- Flexible issue export: Create a Ticket or push to an Import Set table.
To learn more, see Integrating AI Security With ServiceNow.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming Hybrid Workers
body: Introducing support for Hybrid Workers

Customers can now deploy workers inside their own environment and avoid the need to allow any inbound connections. Workers deployed in the customer's environment make outbound connections only back to the AIRT platform and any test prompts/responses stay within the customer's network.

A self-service API documentation portal provides an OpenAPI 3.1 (Swagger) interface with code samples, allowing new API consumers to authenticate and make their first API call independently.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming MCP Security Ratings
body: MCP Security Ratings

MCP Security Ratings is a catalog of well-known public MCP servers that AIRT has already security-tested. Each server gets a letter grade (A to F) so you can judge its risk at a glance, then click in to see exactly which issues were found and why. Note that this feature only covers public MCP servers and not private MCP servers.

entries.title: Azure Container Registry Support for AI Asset Discovery
body: AI Security can now automatically discover and catalog Azure Container Registry (ACR) repositories and their container images. This enables security administrators to gain centralized visibility into AI models, packages, and frameworks embedded in container images across their entire Azure container infrastructure.
To learn more, see Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Container Registry (ACR) Repositories, Managing Services, and IAM Roles and Permissions for Azure.

entries.title: Cross-Console Navigation in AI Security
body: AI Security Admin Portal now supports cross-console navigation, enabling you to navigate directly from the AI Security console to the corresponding resource in your cloud service provider (CSP) console.
As part of this enhancement, changes are made to the following pages:
- AI Infrastructure > AI Assets > MCP Servers
- AI Infrastructure > AI Assets > Agents
- AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Data Stores (S3 bucket, GCP storage, RDS instances, etc.)
- AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Workloads (virtual machine, EC2 instance, etc.)
- AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Guardrails
- AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities
See image.

entries.title: Multi-Cloud Toggle for AI Security
body: Administrators can now switch between cloud environments directly within the AI Security Admin Portal. Previously, administrators could only view data for the cloud assigned to them via Authentication Service, with no option to toggle between clouds. With this update, administrators can seamlessly switch between clouds and view data across all cloud environments from a single interface.
See image.

entries.title: System Logs: AI Infra Scanning
body: Zscaler AI Security introduces a new System Logs page under Administration > System Logs, with an AI Infra Scanning tab that gives administrators a unified, filterable view of every AI infrastructure scan event generated across their AWS, Azure, and GCP environments. The page displays scan outcomes including successes, failures, and detailed error messages, so administrators can quickly triage scan health, identify misconfigurations, and audit the inventory pipeline over time.
See image.
To learn more, see About System Logs - AI Infra Scanning and Downloading Reports.

entries.title: AI Red Teaming Broker Support for Private Applications in AI Security Admin Portal
body: Zscaler AI Security introduces AI Red Teaming (AIRT) Broker, a more secure way to connect AIRT to customer applications without requiring firewall changes.

Previously, customers needed to whitelist AIRT source IP addresses on their firewall to allow red teaming access, a process that introduced both operational overhead and security risk. AIRT Broker eliminates this requirement by establishing inside-out connectivity, removing the need to allow any inbound access on the firewall.

Broker configuration is now manageable directly from the AI Security Admin Portal. Security teams can create and manage brokers, then assign them to specific application targets enabling AI Red Teaming to securely reach internally hosted AI applications without firewall modifications.
You can access the Brokers page from Administration > Red Teaming > Brokers.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding the AI Security Broker, About AI Red Teaming Brokers, Connect an Asset, Registering a Broker, and Configuring a Broker Target,

entries.title: Detection Level Setting for Probes
body: AI Red Teaming introduces the Detection Level setting in probe configuration, giving security teams control over how aggressively a probe flags model responses as failures.
Three detection levels are available:
- Strict: Flags a wider range of potentially problematic outputs, including borderline cases.
- Moderate: Balances sensitivity between strict and permissive thresholds.
- Permissive: Flags only high-severity violations.

entries.title: Import Zscaler Policy
body: AI Red Teaming now includes an AI Guard Tenant ID field in the Import Policy pop-up, streamlining integration with Zscaler AI Guard. Users can specify their tenant ID directly during the policy import process, eliminating the need for additional configuration steps.
See image.

entries.title: Rerun Action for Test Runs
body: AI Red Teaming adds a Rerun action at the test run level, consistent with the existing probe-level rerun behavior.

The Rerun action is available when at least one probe run is incomplete or has ended with errors. When triggered, the current vulnerability assessment resumes by rerunning all incomplete and failed probes without requiring a full test run restart. No additional units are charged for reruns, though results may vary if the test run configuration or probe versions have changed since the original run.

entries.title: Enhanced Identity Inventory: Grouping, Multi-Target Visibility, and Identity Categorization
body: Zscaler AI Security introduces significant improvements to how identities are represented, visualized, and categorized on the AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities page. These enhancements give security teams clearer visibility into cross-cloud identity access and the role each identity plays in the AI ecosystem.
The following enhancements are available in the AI Security Admin Portal:
- New filters and columns on the AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities page:
- Access Category: Categorizes identities based on their access type and AI usage.
- Target Environment: Displays the environments that the identity can access.
- Source Environment: Displays the environments from which the identity originates.
- See image.
- Updated General Information panel:
- The Access Category and Target Environment details are now included in the identity's General Information page.
- See image.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.19.0
body: # Prompt Allowlist

The prompt allowlist for AI Guard allows you to track and manage any prompts that you wish to allow that may otherwise be blocked by an existing AI Guard policy. Prompts added to the allowlist are fully encrypted, so the prompt content remains protected end-to-end.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Prompt Allowlist.
# Detection Details Improvements

When viewing transaction details in the dashboard, the prompt and response fields are grouped into separate rows (Detections / Action / Tags) for clearer, at-a-glance readability. Each detection tag group now expands via the View details link.
See image.

When a prompt contains PII or Secrets, matched spans are highlighted inline in both the original and masked views using action-colored background fills. Hovering a span shows a tooltip with the masked replacement and confidence (e.g. "Masked as: IP_ADDRESS-1 · 73% confidence"), or the original value and confidence in the masked view.
See image.
To learn more, see About Dashboard.
# Prompt Injection Explainability

This release overhauls how flagged Prompt-Injection chunks are surfaced in the Transaction Details view. The previous highlighting is replaced with a more clear approach, a sticky confidence legend makes it easy to navigate flagged chunks, and a new Annotate mode that labels each chunk for precise review.
- Confidence-Tiered Highlighting: Flagged text chunks are now grouped by confidence tier, so you can quickly gauge how strongly each chunk was flagged.
- ≥ 90%: Highest-confidence injection chunks.
- 70–89%: Medium confidence.
- 50–69%: Lower confidence.
- See image.
- Sticky Confidence Legend: A sticky "Prompt injection confidence" legend stays in view while scrolling and only renders the tiers that actually have flagged chunks.
- Click a tier: Clicking on the prompt injection confidence will scroll to the first prompt chunk in that confidence tier. Clicking again cycles to the next chunk.
- See image.
- Hovering over a tier: Dims all other text and non-matching tier labels, isolating the relevant chunks for quick visual scanning.
- See image.

- Annotate Mode: A new Annotate toggle in the legend turns on detailed chunk labeling for side-by-side comparison and reference. Each flagged prompt chunk gets a numbered marker ([1], [2], etc.) at its end and also receives a distinct pastel background color so individual chunks are easy to tell apart.
- See image.
To learn more, see About Dashboard.
# Additional AI Provider
Windsurf is now available as a supported provider.
To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

entries.title: AI Assets - Code Repositories: GitHub Integration
body: Zscaler AI Security Admin Portal introduces GitHub integration for AI Assets - Code Repositories, enabling administrators to automatically discover, inventory, and scan GitHub repositories for AI models, packages, frameworks, and agentic workflows embedded in source code.
As a part of this feature, the following changes are available in the AI Security Admin Portal:

- GitHub repository onboarding: You can connect GitHub to AI Security from Administration > Account Onboarding by selecting Code Repository as the resource type and GitHub as the provider. The onboarding flow uses a GitHub OAuth App to authorize access to selected repositories.

- Automated repository discovery: After authorization, AI Security automatically initiates repository discovery in the background. All discovered repositories are mapped to the Default Business Unit by default and can be reassigned post-discovery.
- Granular scan rule configuration: Configure scan rules to control which repositories are scanned.
To learn more, see Onboarding GitHub Tenant and Configuring Scan Rule for GitHub.

entries.title: Embedded AI Apps Visibility in AI Asset Management
body: Zscaler AI Security Admin Portal expands the AI Asset Management platform to automatically discover and identify Embedded AI applications accessed across your organization. Security and IT teams can now gain visibility into AI-powered features within popular SaaS applications alongside traditional standalone GenAI applications.

This enhancement gives security and IT teams a complete view of their organization's AI footprint, including AI capabilities embedded within everyday SaaS applications. Teams can now strengthen AI governance by monitoring both GenAI and Embedded AI applications from a single platform, while identifying emerging AI adoption trends and shadow AI usage across departments.
See image.
To learn more, see About Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI.

entries.title: Enhancements to AI Security
body: The following enhancements are available in the AI Security platform.
# Public AI Overview
The following widgets are added to the Public AI Overview page:
- Upload Volume: Displays the total volume of data uploaded to public AI applications.
- Download Volume: Displays the total volume of data downloaded from public AI applications.
- Embedded AI Apps: Displays the number of embedded AI applications detected across your environment.
The following widgets are removed from the Public AI Overview page:
- Sensitive Data
- Sensitive Data Transactions
# Usage Insights
A new Locations tab is introduced on the Usage Insights page, enabling administrators to view AI usage insights and drill-downs based on locations.
To learn more, see About Public AI Overview and About Usage Insights.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.18.3
body: # Enhanced Dashboard Visibility

The Dashboard page has been updated to include more granular detection details (Dashboard > Details > Detection Summary), including detected entities and confidence scores. Users can now view comprehensive data for both request and response events, providing deeper insight into trigger conditions.
See image.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Dashboard.
# Policy Configuration & Detector Updates
1. Japanese is now available as an option in the Language detector.
2. The Secrets detector has been enhanced to allow for disabling any unwanted labels from detections.
3. Some upcoming PII labels have been added with only Detect or Disabled actions available at this time.
- The update on existing policies should be on the PII detector configuration page.
- See image.

- Existing policies must be manually updated to move the updated labels to Disabled mode. Ensure that both Request and Response policies are updated with any small change (e.g., updating a Severity label) before saving so that the new label updates appear.
To learn more, see Adding and Managing AI Guard Policy Configurations.
# Enhancements & Bug Fixes
- Dashboard: Optimized page load times for the event dashboard across all operating modes.

- Proxy Changes in User Mode: The Request Blocking message for Claude has been updated in browsers when there is no custom message. The expected message behavior is: "This request has been blocked by your organization."

entries.title: Activity-Based Detection for AWS Bedrock Model Inventory
body: The AI Security Asset Management platform now utilizes activity-based detection to precisely identify managed and custom AWS Bedrock models currently utilized by your organization. By analyzing AWS CloudTrail events, the inventory only includes models accessed within the preceding 90 days, ensuring data hygiene and accuracy.
Security teams can now access two granular perspectives for each identified model on the AI Security - Models page (AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - Models):
- Usage Timeline: Provides visibility into the 10 most recent invocations, detailing activity trends and specific timestamps.
- Top 10 Users: Lists the primary unique identities, including user names and IAM roles, along with invocation counts and last seen data.
To learn more, see About AI Assets - Models.

entries.title: Export Report Option
body: Report export is now supported on the following pages in AI Security Admin Portal:
- AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - Models
- AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - MCP Servers
- AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - Agents
- AI Infrastructure > AI Resources - Data Stores
- AI Infrastructure > AI Resources - Workloads
- AI Infrastructure > AI Resources - Guardrails
- AI Infrastructure > AI Resources - Identities
- AI Infrastructure > Issues > Issues View
- AI Infrastructure > Issues > Model Scan Findings

entries.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio Support in AI Security
body: Zscaler AI Security now supports Microsoft Copilot Studio, enabling organizations to automatically discover and secure AI agents built on the platform. This integration helps security teams proactively identify and remediate misconfigurations that could expose sensitive data across agentic AI workflows.
With this release, AI Security introduces the following capabilities:

- Automated Agent Discovery: Automatically discovers and maintains a unified inventory of agents deployed across Copilot Studio environments, along with their associated MCP servers and knowledge bases.
- Security Posture Assessment: Identifies and evaluates the security risks associated with Copilot Studio agents.
- Entitlement Visibility: Provides clear visibility into who has access to each Copilot Studio agent.
To learn more, see Onboarding Microsoft Copilot Studio Tenant.

entries.title: RAG Processing Initiated from App Configuration
body: Zscaler AI Security now initiates RAG processing directly from the App Configuration page when users click Complete or Update, providing a visual progress indicator throughout the process.

Users can navigate away from the configuration screen while processing continues in the background, streamlining the overall workflow. To maintain data consistency, the system prevents new test runs from starting until RAG processing is complete and disables RAG file updates while a test run is in progress.

entries.title: Standalone Prompt Hardening in AI Red Teaming
body: The following changes are made as a part of this enhancement:
# Prompt Hardening Support for Standalone AI Applications
Zscaler AI Security introduces Standalone App Hardening, enabling security teams to extend prompt hardening to applications that are not yet integrated into the Zscaler AI Security asset ecosystem.

Previously, prompt hardening was only available to fully onboarded applications, leaving unmanaged and shadow apps without AI-driven security coverage. From the AI Infrastructure > Remediation page, security teams can now manually enter an application name and associate it with a business unit to generate hardened prompts without completing the standard onboarding process. This ensures that unmanaged and shadow apps receive the same AI-driven security intelligence as fully onboarded applications, giving your team consistent protection across your entire application environment.
See image.
# Prompt Hardening Available Without Probe Prerequisite
Zscaler AI Security removes the mandatory probe requirement for prompt hardening, enabling security teams to activate baseline hardening instructions from day one of onboarding.

Previously, applying prompt hardening policies required customers to onboard an application and complete a probe run first, delaying initial AI Security coverage. Probe runs and prompt hardening are now fully decoupled, allowing security teams to activate baseline hardening instructions immediately upon onboarding, apply hardening policies without completing probe configuration, and begin securing AI applications from the first day of deployment.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.17.0
body: # Additional AI Provider
Mistral Vibe (formerly Le Chat) is now available as a supported provider. To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.16.0
body: # Gemini CLI Support in Proxy Mode
Google Gemini (command-line interface) CLI support is now available for AI Guard in Proxy mode. To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.
# Additional AI Provider
Bedrock Anthropic support for traffic is now available in User mode. To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.
# Enhancements & Bug Fixes
- Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Misc. enhancements and bug fixes.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.15.1
body: # Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Management

AI Guard 2.15.1 introduces enhanced data integration capabilities and significantly expands administrative control through advanced Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). These updates are designed to strengthen governance, flexibility, and operational visibility for enterprise environments. Previously, the only supported roles were Administrator, Editor, and Viewer.
See image.
RBAC management includes:
- Support for custom roles and permissions, replacing the previous fixed role model.
- Fine-grained access control over administrative functions.
- Ability to tailor permissions based on organizational needs and responsibilities.
To learn more, see Managing Role-Based Access Control in AI Guard.
# Azure Data Explorer (ADX) Log Export Support
AI Guard now supports seamless integration with Azure Data Explorer (ADX), enabling efficient export and analysis of event data.
See image.
Key capabilities include:
- Streaming event metadata and content directly to ADX via Azure Event Hub.
- Enabling advanced analytics, querying, and long-term data storage.
- Improve visibility into AI activity, policy enforcement, and system behavior.
- Support scalable and high-performance data ingestion pipelines.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.14.2
body: # Codex Application Support

Support added for the Codex application. Codex is an OpenAI code agent and doesn't require additional Internet & SaaS (ZIA) configuration for URLs if you've already configured the forwarding for ChatGPT traffic from ZIA. It supports request blocking and response blocking.
# Additional AI Provider
GitHub Copilot is now available as a supported provider for prompt visibility and blocking. Response inspection is not yet supported.
To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.
# Tenant Setting Additions
From the Tenant Settings page in AI Guard, you are now able to:
- View your AWS Account ID in the General tab. This is used for optional AWS integrations such as log exports to AWS S3 buckets or optional AWS customer-managed keys for encryption.
- Start a manual sync with ZIA outside the scheduled batch window in the Integrations tab.
To learn more, see Managing Tenant Settings and Managing AI Guard Log Exports.
# Enhancements & Bug Fixes
- Microsoft 365 & Copilot:
- M365 Response Blocking: Added support for response blocking cases.
- M365 Response Blocking Options Hidden: M365 default suggestions won't appear for a response blocking use case.
- Copilot Think Deeper Mode: Added support for consistent responses in Think Deeper Mode.
- ChatGPT Message Behavior: Added support to ensure ChatGPT generally follows configured custom or standard block messaging.
- UI Enhancement: Changes to a policy that have occurred since its creation are now displayed as an entry on the Audit Log page.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.13.1
body: # Default LLM Provider Auto-Provisioning
During AI Guard tenant creation, all default LLM providers are now:
- Automatically provisioned.
- Pre-configured and ready to use.
This eliminates the need for manual setup, reduces operational overhead, and accelerates start-up time. This has no impact on existing customers.
# Additional AI Provider
ElevenLabs (text-to-speech mode) is now available as a supported provider.
To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.
# Enhancements & Bug Fixes
- Microsoft 365 Response Truncation: Resolved an issue where responses were being truncated unexpectedly on the dashboard page.
- Claude API Error with PII Masking: Fixed a bug causing 400 errors when PII masking was enabled in Claude-code usage workflows.
- Dashboard Filter Dropdown Issue: Resolved an issue where not all filter options were visible in dashboard dropdown menus.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.12.0
body: # Intellectual Property (IP) Detector

The IP Detector is a critical new feature designed to safeguard proprietary or sensitive information provided by users as background data (the "context") for language model interactions. It analyzes a user's subsequent input/query against the provided context to determine if the input is semantically similar enough to indicate a potential leak, paraphrase, or direct exposure of the sensitive source material.
This ensures that the original context is protected from being inadvertently or maliciously recycled through the input prompt itself.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding and Managing AI Guard Policy Configurations.
# Additional PII Chart Insights
On the Insights page, when users click on a specific bar in a PII graph, a pop-up window will appear with all transactions that contributed to that bar in the chart.
See image.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Insights.
# Support for Disabling Policy Actions in PII Detectors

In addition to the Allow, Block, and Detect options for policy actions, PII detectors have the ability to Disable policy actions. If a label is selected as Disabled, it is not covered under PII detections.
The "Person's name" label is defaulted to Disabled.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding and Managing AI Guard Policy Configurations.
# Filter Log Exports with Prompt Action
Log Exports now allow filtering logs based on prompt actions. The new policy filtering options are Export Allowed/Detected Prompts and Export Blocked Prompts.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.
# Additional AI Providers
The following AI applications have been added as supported providers.
- Napkin AI (.app.napkin.ai)
- DeepAI (.api.deepai.org)
- Google Gemini Enterprise (.biz-discoveryengine.googleapis.com,
- .discoveryengine.clients6.google.com)
- OpenCode (.opencode.ai)
- Gamma (.api.gamma.app, ai.api.gamma.app)
- Builder.io (.api.builder.io, .cdn.builder.io, .cdn.builder.codes)
To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.
# Chat History Deletion
In the Tenant Settings Security tab, you have the option to automatically delete chat history of response blocking cases for providers like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Tenant Settings.
# Enhancements & Bug Fixes
- Implemented auto ordering of rule execution within policy controls to prevent conflict errors and ensure consistent policy enforcement.
- The default detection threshold for PII has been updated to 0.5.
- AI Guard now supports dual-mode login, enabling both Authentication Service and email-based authentication.
- Logos updated for providers.

entries.title: AI Guard 2.11.0
body: # Additional Masking Capability
Enhanced data privacy with extended masking options on Dashboard and LLM providers. For more information on how the options work, see the following table:
| PII Flag on Product | Send Masked PII to LLM | Expected Behavior |
| Disable | Disable | Actual PII content is visible on Dashboard (no masking) and is sent to the LLM. |
| Enable | Disable | The AI Guard Dashboard should show the masked content. The actual, not masked PII content is sent to the LLM. |
| Enable | Enable | The AI Guard Dashboard should show the masked content. The masked PII content is sent to the LLM. |
# Dashboard and Insights Export PDF Option
Users can export reports directly in PDF format from the Dashboard and Insights pages.
See image.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Dashboard and About AI Guard Insights.
# Additional User Mode Providers

MaxAI (api.maxai.me), Lovable (api.lovable.dev), Bolt (bolt.new), and Google Gemini Code (*.gemini.google.com and cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com) have been added as supported providers in User mode. Only request blocking is supported on these new providers.
To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.
# Bug Fixes
- Minor bug fix around allowing All Application option as a policy control criteria.
- Updated Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) Ingester service changes: Added compatibility with ZIA APIs.
- Resolved User mode traffic message truncation issues for ALLOW cases:
- OpenAI
- Perplexity

entries.title: AI Guard 2.10.0
body: # Splunk Integration for Logs

AI Guard now supports Splunk integration, enabling seamless export and monitoring of logs within Splunk environments. This enhances observability, security monitoring, and centralized log analysis capabilities.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.
# Google Gemini Workspace Support (Initial Release)
Google Gemini (Workspace version) is now a new User Mode Provider, enabling monitoring and policy enforcement for Gemini usage within Google Docs.
# Enhanced PII Detection Visualizations
The Insights page in AI Guard has introduced new graphical elements to improve the visibility of:
- PII detections
- PII categories
- Additional detection variations
See image.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Insights.
# Improved Audit Log Diff Visibility
Audit Logs now display the actual entity-level diff, allowing administrators to clearly see what changes were made by users. This significantly improves traceability and change auditing.
# Bug Fixes
- Minor bug fix around allowing All Application option as a policy control criteria.
- Updated ZIA Ingester service changes: Added compatibility with ZIA APIs.
- Resolved User Mode traffic message truncation issues for ALLOW cases:
- OpenAI
- Perplexity
